identity_evidence.quote: We present the case of a patient with Crohn’s disease who experienced recurrent pneumothorax after starting treatment with ustekinumab
A 17-year-old boy, diagnosed with ileocolic Crohn’s disease

attribution_limitations: The abstract places the new Crohn’s disease flare-up "One year later" (after the sentence on resolution of the first pneumothorax), while the case text dates it to April 2023. The abstract gives no anchor date (the resolution and withdrawal are undated), so the two are not demonstrably contradictory; the abstract interval is approximate. Recorded as an ambiguity: the dated case-text fact is included and the abstract timing is review_only.

Authors first judged a low probability that ustekinumab caused the pneumothorax, then after the recurrence considered the drug can be related to it. These are sequential author judgments with more evidence called for, not a documented diagnosis of drug-induced pneumothorax.
The paradoxical psoriasis is called treatment-related without naming the treatment in that sentence.
Dates, side of the chest drain and duration between the drain, CT, surgery and ustekinumab withdrawal are not stated.
The second discontinuation of ustekinumab is implied only by "both resolving after discontinuation of the drug"; no separate sentence states when it was stopped.
